To address this challenge, this paper presents ALISTA, an algorithm\u2013hardware co-design framework for efficient attention computation that achieves a superior trade-off between accuracy and scalability.ALISTA adopts a hybrid sparse attention strategy that combines exact attention within fixed local windows and approximate global attention using norm-ranging Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH)-based Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS). Relevant global keys are efficiently identified by formulating attention as a MIPS problem and solving it using an LSH scheme that mitigates norm sensitivity through subset partitioning and multi-probe ranking. Algorithmic evaluation on the Long Range Arena benchmark achieves an average accuracy of 53.16%, exceeding Reformer by 2.49%, while maintaining linear scaling with sequence length.On the hardware side, the proposed accelerator features a novel output-stationary hexagonally connected systolic array optimized for maximizing data reuse. Sparsity induced by the attention mechanism is efficiently exploited using a CSR-based matrix multiplier. Prototyping on an iWave Xilinx XCZU7CG platform operating at 250 MHz achieves up to 8.5$\\times$ higher throughput, reduces latency to 0.67$\\times$ that of dense self-attention for long-context sequences, and improves the Energy\u2013Delay Product by up to 31$\\times$ relative to dense Transformer and Nystr\u00f6mformer
